problem: Audio-visual navigation agents (SoundSpaces, SAVi) cannot ask for help and fail when sounds are sporadic, unheard or masked by distractors. Prior interactive-navigation work decides when to query with heuristics (action-probability gaps, hand-made lost conditions) or only at fixed locations, and uses restricted oracle feedback.
motivation: Real-world navigation is audio-visual, uncertain and time-critical, so an agent should know when it is uncertain and ask a human for short free-form language guidance, but with a limited query budget. Asking too often costs autonomy; asking too rarely leaves the agent wandering after the sound stops.
key_idea: A hierarchical options RL framework in which a high-level policy learns, via a query-penalizing reward, when to query an oracle, and two low-level policies either navigate from audio-visual cues or follow the oracle's natural-language instruction.
insight: Learning when to query matters more than the language architecture: the learned πq beats Random, Uniform and Model-Uncertainty triggers in both Table 2 (language feedback) and Table 3 (GT-action feedback), and it spreads queries across the episode instead of exhausting the budget early. Swapping the π_ℓ architecture (GloVe/CLIP, GRU/Transformer, Table 4) always stays above SAVi, so the gain comes from the querying framework. The gap between language feedback (36.1 SR) and GT actions (48.2 SR) shows that the language-following policy is the bottleneck.
method: Task/POMDP: SAVi-style semantic audio-goal navigation with an added query action, a limited query budget (K=3), and an oracle that returns a short natural-language instruction. Objective: maximize return minus a query penalty ζ.

High-level query policy πq: Transformer encoder-decoder actor-critic over the observation memory (150 steps) and goal estimate. It picks between the audio-goal option πg and the language option π_ℓ, and is trained with DD-PPO.

Audio-goal policy πg: SAVi-like Transformer encoder-decoder with a goal descriptor network (location plus category estimate, fused with pose change). Trained in two stages: without memory, then with memory and frozen encoders.

Language policy π_ℓ: a Transformer T1 encodes the observation and goal, the result is fused with the CLIP embedding of the instruction through an FC layer, and a second Transformer T2 over past beliefs gives the actions. It runs for ν=3 steps per query, is pre-trained by imitation on fine-grained instructions from Hong et al. (sub-instruction aware VLN, R2R-derived), then fine-tuned on-policy with shortest-path teacher actions.

Query reward: ζq penalizes each query, with a form that changes once k passes the budget K (rneg=-1.2), plus ζf=-0.5 for queries made within τ steps of the previous one. πg is rewarded +1 for reducing geodesic distance, +10 for success and -0.01 per step.

Oracle instruction generation: the oracle takes the shortest-path segment of n=4 observation-action pairs and uses a Speaker LSTM encoder-decoder (Fried et al.), trained on R2R instruction-trajectory pairs, to generate the natural-language instruction at any grid location.

setting.backbone: Transformer encoder-decoder actor-critics (πq, πg, π_ℓ) trained from scratch with DD-PPO and imitation; frozen CLIP text encoder for instructions; LSTM Speaker model as oracle
setting.training_data: SAVi semantic audio-visual navigation dataset (0.5M train episodes, 85 Matterport3D scans, 21 sound categories); R2R-derived fine-grained instructions (Hong et al.) for pre-training π_ℓ and Speaker; ~22M RL steps for πq
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (64x64), binaural audio spectrogram (65x26), pose relative to start, previous action, language instruction upon query
setting.action_space: low-level discrete on a 1 m grid: stop, move_forward, turn_left, turn_right, plus a query option
setting.privileged: An oracle with shortest-path knowledge to the goal supplies the instructions (or GT actions in the upper-bound variant); no other privileged information

numbers_note: The paper does not name the split in its tables; the 1000-episode test split is assumed ("There are 0.5M/500/1000 episodes ... train/val/test"). Test environments are unseen. The distractor results appear in a figure-embedded table (Fig. 3a).
results: With language feedback and at most 3 queries, AVLEN reaches SR 36.1 (heard) and 26.2 (unheard), versus 33.9 and 24.8 for the best baseline SAVi; under distractors it reaches 14.0 versus 11.8. With GT-action feedback it reaches 48.2 and 36.7. The learned query policy also beats Random, Uniform and Model-Uncertainty triggers in all settings.
limitations: Depends on a strong language-following policy π_ℓ and a pre-trained Speaker oracle whose instructions can be irrelevant or wrong; the gap to GT-action feedback is large.
Language gains are modest (+1.4 to +2.2 SR) and evaluated only in simulation with a synthetic oracle; English-only data and mostly North American Matterport3D houses.
